description: Host-side retry policy: the pure state machine in packages/core/src/roomLifecycle.ts (LiveKitRoomLifecycle), mirroring the six tests in packages/core/tests/roomLifecycle.test.ts. This is a HELPER, not engine behaviour, and the distinction is the point: per spec §10 the engine performs NO retries — it classifies an ending, emits it, and stops. Retry lives here so a policy bug is fixed in one host without a package release, and so the server-side guards see honest client behaviour. This is the policy Penthouse Pets settled on after an auto-reconnecting client opened 864 sessions in 48 hours; a host that wants different policy simply does not use the class. It is vectored because the admission rules ARE the incident fix, and a Dart port that got the latch wrong would reproduce the incident rather than the fix. Four rules are decisions: (1) `agent-ended` never auto-retries — it returns await-user and does NOT spend an attempt, because a departed renderer means the slot went somewhere and hammering it just burns the budget; (2) `rate-limited` LATCHES, so every later failure is blocked until a real user gesture clears it, which is what stops a 429 from becoming a retry loop; (3) installing a replacement owner does NOT reset the episode, but the new room actually RENDERING does — reaching a renderer is the only evidence that a retry worked; (4) `release` is owner-gated and serialises on a disconnect barrier, so a stale owner cannot tear down its replacement and a host cannot mint a new room while the old one is still billing. ADMISSION CONTROL ONLY: a counter and a latch. No backoff, no timers — pacing a retry is host code, and nothing here sleeps. Scenario shape: `steps` is replayed in order against one instance built with `maxAutomaticRetries` (default 3). Owners are named by STRING, and the runner maps each distinct name to a distinct object identity — that is how the identity semantics (`isCurrent`, the stale-owner rules) get expressed without putting object references in JSON. `expectResults` is the per-step return value, null for steps that return nothing. `expectFinal` reports the instance getters plus a per-owner count of how many times its disconnect callback actually ran. `expectOrder` is for the one scenario about ordering.

scenarios.name: a_replacement_waits_for_the_owned_room_disconnect_barrier
scenarios.comment: The ordering that protects the participant-minute budget: the old room must be fully down before a host mints its replacement. A host that fetched a token first would hold two rooms, both billing. `gated` makes the disconnect hang until `openGate`, so "waited" is distinguishable from "happened to be fast".

scenarios.name: only_three_automatic_terminal_replacements_are_admitted
scenarios.comment: The bound is the whole point; the fourth failure is refused.

scenarios.name: the_retry_bound_is_the_constructed_one
scenarios.comment: Pins that maxAutomaticRetries is honoured rather than hardcoded at 3 — a port that ignored the argument passes the row above and fails here.

scenarios.name: installing_a_replacement_does_not_reset_the_episode_but_rendering_does
scenarios.comment: Swapping in a new room is not evidence that anything got better; only a renderer actually painting is. Resetting on install would make the attempt bound unreachable and restore the 864-session behaviour.

scenarios.name: a_stale_owner_cannot_reset_the_episode_by_reporting_a_renderer
scenarios.comment: The old room finishing its warmup after it was replaced is a real race. It reports false and changes nothing.

scenarios.name: agent_ended_waits_for_explicit_user_action_instead_of_auto_respawning
scenarios.comment: And it spends NO attempt: the episode budget is for transport failures, which a retry can plausibly fix.

scenarios.name: a_rate_limit_latches_and_blocks_the_episode_until_a_user_gesture
scenarios.comment: The one that matters most. Without the latch a 429 becomes a retry loop against a server that is already telling us to stop.

scenarios.name: the_rate_limit_latch_survives_a_replacement_owner
scenarios.comment: The latch is episode state, not room state. A host that swapped rooms to escape it would be doing exactly what it exists to prevent.

scenarios.name: a_stale_owner_cannot_release_a_replacement
scenarios.comment: Release is owner-gated. The old mount calling release after it was replaced must not tear down the room the user is currently looking at.
